t: Code Ownership Mapper - Signature build-tool concept
title: Code Ownership Mapper - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Identifies responsibility for components or files.
description:
Code Ownership Mapper is the Signature build-tool concept that identifies responsibility for components or files. In the Signature line, it is not a loose collection of scripts but a deterministic capability: the same build request produces the same verified result on every run, on every machine. This database documents the concept in full - what it is, the seven framework pillars that implement it, the real techniques it stands on, the standards it honors, and laddered drills that teach it from first principles to compounded mastery.

An AI that builds on demand needs Code Ownership Mapper the way a workshop needs its central bench. Without it, every build becomes improvisation: requirements drift, steps run out of order, and nobody can say why a result came out the way it did. With it, the build becomes a protocol - inputs declared, transformations explicit, outputs checked against the original request. That protocol is what these records describe, pillar by pillar.

Every record in this database carries a runnable demonstration program, because a build tool that cannot show its work cannot be trusted with real work. Read the overview, study the pillars, practice the drills, and run the demos: by the end the Code Ownership Mapper will be a capability you can invoke, not a concept you have read about.

t: Signature Chronicler - Code Ownership Mapper framework pillar
title: Signature Chronicler - Code Ownership Mapper framework pillar
definition: The Chronicler component of the Signature Code Ownership Mapper framework, owning chronicler. Signature concept.
description:
The Chronicler is a load-bearing component of the Signature Code Ownership Mapper framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's chronicler responsibilities belongs to the Chronicler, and the Chronicler answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Chronicler can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Chronicler works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Code Ownership Mapper charter (identifies responsibility for components or files.). The Chronicler reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small vcs job that needs Code Ownership Mapper. The Chronicler takes the request's chronicler responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Chronicler's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Code Ownership Mapper. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Merger - Code Ownership Mapper framework pillar
title: Signature Merger - Code Ownership Mapper framework pillar
definition: The Merger component of the Signature Code Ownership Mapper framework, owning merger. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Code Ownership Mapper framework, the Merger owns the framework's merger responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Merger's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Merger from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Identifies responsibility for components or files.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Version control and change management build needs Code Ownership Mapper, so the framework invokes the Merger on the the framework's merger responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

t: Signature Brancher - Code Ownership Mapper framework pillar
title: Signature Brancher - Code Ownership Mapper framework pillar
definition: The Brancher component of the Signature Code Ownership Mapper framework, owning brancher. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Code Ownership Mapper framework decomposes the capability (Identifies responsibility for components or files.) into seven pillars, and the Brancher is the one that owns the framework's brancher responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Code Ownership Mapper result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Brancher's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Brancher's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Code Ownership Mapper. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.
